q1_issues.issue: 'freshly' is recorded as (Degree sk_layer_1 poured freshly), but Degree's level slot is for intensifiers/downtoners (very, slightly, fairly) or the fixed construction markers — 'freshly' is a manner/time adverb, not a degree.
'from beneath a layer' is flattened to Source on the layer, dropping 'beneath', so the parse says the bodies came out of the layer rather than from underneath it.

The light verb 'performed' is dropped and the autopsy noun is used directly as the eventuality; the light-verb collapse is stated only for intransitive occur/happen/take place, so the surface verb is lost without licence.

q2_gaps: transitive light-verb + event-noun ('performed an autopsy', 'made a decision') — the light-verb rule covers only occur / happen / took place, leaving no ruling on whether the matrix verb is reified
portion / material of-phrase ('a layer of concrete', 'a cup of water') — explicitly excluded from the genitive mapping but given no positive encoding
an adverb modifying a participial adjective on an entity ('freshly poured') — Manner is an event role and there is no event, so no slot exists
complex preposition 'from beneath' on an event — the named role Source and the multi-word preposition-joining rule (FromBeneath) both claim it, with no tie-breaker
a partitive over an indefinite set ('one of three bodies') — the partitive trigger is 'of the / of these / of those / of them'
notes: The lowercase-adjective-before-a-place-name handling of 'a northwest Indiana home' follows the sub-region rule exactly (witness, Member northwest, LocatedIn indiana, Name atom), and the reduced relative 'recovered from …' is correctly given the event form.
